h1:
Phetchabun–Loei: 3 Days, 2 Nights
The Winter Mountain Route
intro: Winter is when these mountains look their best, and once you've made it to Phetchabun, driving on into Loei is only another two or three hours — well worth it. This route strings together the standout peaks of both provinces into a single trip. You start at Khao Kho for the morning sea of mist, climb Phu Thap Boek, the highest point in Phetchabun, cross over to Phu Ruea (the coldest spot in Thailand), and finish at Chiang Khan, the old town on the Mekong. We've laid out a relaxed self-drive timeline with no rush, plus real distances and food to eat along the way.

blocks.html: The Phetchabun–Loei route is a great fit for a winter road trip, because the signature peaks of both provinces line up along the same north–south corridor — no long detours. Most people start at Khao Kho (about 580–590 km from Bangkok, a 6–7 hour drive), then work their way north into Loei. The distances between towns aren't long, but it's winding mountain road, so build in extra time and drive during daylight.

blocks.title: Best time to go
blocks.html: November to January is peak season for the sea of mist and cool-weather flowers. Morning temperatures on Phu Ruea can drop close to 0°C. Late rainy/early cool season (October) brings thick mist but still some rain. If you're going in high winter, book your Khao Kho and Chiang Khan stays several weeks ahead — they fill up fast.
Before the day-by-day plan, here's the core distance framework to help you time your driving. These are approximate distances along the actual roads, not straight lines.

items: Bangkok → Khao Kho — about 580–590 km via Highway 21 (Saraburi–Lom Sak), a 6–7 hour drive.
Khao Kho → Phu Thap Boek — about 40–50 km via Lom Sak–Lom Kao, a 1–1.5 hour drive, steep near the top.
Khao Kho/Lom Sak → Phu Ruea (Loei) — about 110–130 km, a 2–2.5 hour drive through Dan Sai.
Phu Ruea → Chiang Khan — about 90–100 km, a 1.5–2 hour drive through Loei town.
Chiang Khan → Bangkok — about 560 km, a 7–8 hour drive via Highway 201/21.

blocks.title: About the car
blocks.html: The final climb up Phu Thap Boek is very steep. A sedan can make it, but you'll need low gear and good brakes. If you're not confident, local songthaews/trucks will take you up from the parking area below. Fill the tank before heading into the mountains — gas stations are fairly spread out.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Khao Kho, sea of mist and a temple on the hill

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, head for Phetchabun on Highway 21
items.note: Leave around 5–6 a.m. and you'll reach Khao Kho by midday. Stop for a meal in Lom Sak or Phetchabun town along the way.

items.activity: Check in around Khao Kho–Khaem Son, drop your bags, then head out
items.note: Pick a place with a valley view so you can hope for morning mist the next day.

items.activity: Phra That Pha Son Kaew (Wat Pha Son Kaew), Ban Thang Daeng
items.note: A mosaic-tiled stupa on a hilltop around 900 m up, with a wide valley view. Dress modestly; go in the afternoon when the sun isn't harsh.

items.activity: Khao Kho Wind Turbine Field, 360-degree viewpoint
items.note: At around 1,050 m, you can see all the way to Pha Son Kaew. A popular spot for golden-hour photos.

items.activity: Settle into a mountain-view café for the cool breeze
items.note: Khao Kho has plenty of valley-view cafés along the main road. Pick one facing west to catch the sunset.

items.activity: Dinner around Khao Kho–Khaem Son, then rest
items.note: Winter nights here are genuinely cold, so bring a warm jacket. You'll need a very early start tomorrow.

blocks.title: Morning sea of mist
blocks.html: The prime window for Khao Kho's sea of mist is around 5–6 a.m., when low mist blankets the valley. Set an alarm. The favorite spots are the wind turbine field and the roadside viewpoints along the Khao Kho road. On a clear morning you'll see it well, but some mornings you'll miss it — it comes down to luck and the weather.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Phu Thap Boek, then crossing to Phu Ruea

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phu Thap Boek → Phu Ruea (crossing into Loei)

items.activity: Wake up for the morning sea of mist at Khao Kho
items.note: If the sky is clear today, stay and watch the mist for a while before packing up.

items.activity: Leave Khao Kho, climb Phu Thap Boek via Lom Kao
items.note: About 40–50 km. The final stretch is very steep, so drive slowly. Phu Thap Boek is the highest point in Phetchabun, around 1,768 m.

items.activity: Terraced cabbage fields and Phu Thap Boek viewpoint, photos of the sea of mist
items.note: In winter you get both mist and tiers of green cabbage fields. It's noticeably colder than Khao Kho.

items.activity: Come down from Phu Thap Boek, back to Lom Sak, lunch
items.note: Lom Sak has noodle shops and local food to refuel before the long drive.

items.activity: Drive into Loei, through Dan Sai, toward Phu Ruea
items.note: About 110–130 km from the Lom Sak area, a 2–2.5 hour drive. It's beautiful mountain road the whole way.

items.activity: Check in around Phu Ruea
items.note: Phu Ruea is a small district, with lodging spread along the main road and hillsides. Pick something near the park entrance to make tomorrow easier.

items.activity: Stroll a vineyard or cool-weather flower garden around Phu Ruea
items.note: Phu Ruea has several wineries and cool-weather flower gardens open for walking and photos. Sip a coffee in the cool air.

items.activity: Dinner in Phu Ruea town, then rest
items.note: Tonight is the coldest of the trip. Pack a heavy jacket and socks — you'll be up early to climb Phu Ruea's summit.

blocks.title: Up to Phu Ruea's summit
blocks.html: Phu Ruea National Park is open roughly 05:00–20:00. Entry is 200 THB for Thai adults, 100 THB for children, and 30 THB per car. The main sunrise spots are Pha Lon Noi and Decho viewpoint. To catch the sunrise, leave your accommodation before dawn, drive up, then walk a short way.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Phu Ruea's summit, then down to Chiang Khan

items.activity: Climb Phu Ruea's summit, watch the sunrise at Pha Lon Noi
items.note: The coldest spot in Thailand — winter mornings can bring frost. Wear a heavy jacket and bring gloves.

items.activity: Come down from Phu Ruea, breakfast, pack up and set off
items.note: Before leaving Phu Ruea, you can stop for more photos at the signs and roadside viewpoints.

items.activity: Drive to Chiang Khan, passing through Loei town
items.note: About 90–100 km, a 1.5–2 hour drive. Stop in Loei town for souvenirs or lunch.

items.activity: Arrive in Chiang Khan, check into a wooden riverside guesthouse (if staying over)
items.note: If you're doing 3 days/2 nights without staying in Chiang Khan, do the afternoon–evening sights, then drive back. Adding a 4th day is more relaxed.

items.activity: Chiang Khan Skywalk (Phra Yai Phu Khok Ngiu), Pak Tom subdistrict
items.note: A glass walkway about 100 m long overlooking where the Hueang River meets the Mekong. Open roughly 07:00–18:00.

items.activity: Kaeng Khut Khu on the Mekong, try Chiang Khan's coconut candy
items.note: A rocky rapid in the middle of the Mekong, clearly visible when the water is low. There are souvenir shops and snacks along the road.

items.activity: Walk Chiang Khan's walking street (Chai Khong Road)
items.note: Lively every evening in winter, with food, souvenirs, and cafés in old wooden houses. A long stroll with the breeze off the Mekong.

items.activity: Dinner by the river, stay over or start the drive back
items.note: If you stay the night in Chiang Khan, the morning sticky-rice alms-giving along the street is the town's signature image.

blocks.text: Where else to stop if you have extra time

blocks.html: If you stretch the trip to 4 days or want to tweak the route, these are stops not far off the main line. Add them depending on your energy and time.

items.name: Phu Pa Po (the Fuji of Loei), Nong Hin district
items.blurb: A viewpoint over Phu Hor, a flat-topped peak that resembles Mount Fuji. Ride a community farm tractor up for a 360-degree view; winter brings a sea of mist.

items.name: Suan Hin Pha Ngam (the Kunming of Loei), Nong Hin district
items.blurb: Pointed limestone hills arranged like Kunming, with walking trails and short boat rides. A good stop if you're driving the Loei–Khon Kaen route.

items.name: Phu Hin Rong Kla (Phetchabun–Phitsanulok border)
items.blurb: Cracked-stone fields, Pha Chu Thong cliff, and mountain history. Winter brings wild Himalayan cherry blossoms. It's on the Phu Thap Boek side, so you can add it to Day 2.

items.name: Loei town–Phra That Si Song Rak, Dan Sai
items.blurb: An old stupa symbolizing friendship, sitting between Phu Ruea and Chiang Khan. Stop to pay respects as you drive through Dan Sai.

blocks.text: Food along the way you shouldn't miss

blocks.html: This trip involves long drives, so the food along the way is the reward. Here are the standouts you can actually find at each stop.

items.name: Lom Sak noodles
items.blurb: The bold, brothy noodles of Lom Sak district — a classic refueling meal before climbing Phu Thap Boek or crossing into Loei.

items.name: Lom Kao khanom chin
items.blurb: Fresh rice noodles from Lom Kao, served with a choice of curries. A local specialty in the foothills before the climb up Phu Thap Boek.

items.name: Hmong food on Phu Thap Boek
items.blurb: Several restaurants atop Phu Thap Boek serve Hmong dishes and highland food, with cabbage-field views to go with it.
items.meta: Phu Thap Boek, Phetchabun · on the mountain

items.name: Phetchabun sweet tamarind
items.blurb: The province's standout souvenir — sweet and meaty. You can find it from Phetchabun town all the way to roadside shops on Highway 21.

items.name: Phu Ruea wine and grapes
items.blurb: Phu Ruea grows grapes for wine. You can walk the vineyards and take home fresh grapes, grape juice, and local wine.

items.name: Loei pork crackling and moo yor
items.blurb: Isan/Loei-style souvenirs, easy to find in Loei town and along the road before Chiang Khan.

items.name: Chiang Khan coconut candy
items.blurb: Chiang Khan's signature souvenir — coconut flesh coated in colored sugar. Find it around Kaeng Khut Khu and the walking street.

items.name: Khao piak sen and riverside coffee in Chiang Khan
items.blurb: Chiang Khan's light breakfast is khao piak sen (rice noodle soup), followed by coffee in an old wooden-house café with the Mekong breeze.

blocks.title: Sticky-rice alms-giving in Chiang Khan
blocks.html: If you stay the night in Chiang Khan, there's a pre-dawn tradition of offering sticky rice to monks along Chai Khong Road. Many guesthouses prepare a sticky-rice set for you. Follow the local rhythm, stay respectful, and don't block the line of monks.

items: Serious warm clothing — mornings on Phu Ruea and Phu Thap Boek get very cold. Pack a hat, gloves, and thick socks.
Check the car — brakes and tires — the mountain roads are winding and steep, especially the climb up Phu Thap Boek.
Fill the tank before the mountains — gas stations are spread out. Plan to refuel in Lom Sak and Loei town.
Book accommodation ahead — Khao Kho, Phu Ruea, and Chiang Khan fill up fast in winter. Book several weeks before you go.
Carry cash — small shops, markets, and some park entrance fees are easier to handle with cash.

faq.q: How many days do you need for this Phetchabun–Loei route?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is enough to cover Khao Kho, Phu Thap Boek, Phu Ruea, and touch Chiang Khan in the afternoon–evening. But if you want to stay a night in Chiang Khan to walk the night market and do the morning alms-giving, stretch it to 4 days/3 nights so it doesn't feel rushed.

faq.q: Can you drive this route in a sedan?
faq.a: Almost all of it, yes. The main roads are good paved roads. The spot to watch out for is the very steep climb up Phu Thap Boek — a sedan can make it, but you'll need low gear and brakes in good condition. If you're not confident, local songthaews will take you up from the parking area below.

faq.q: Is Loei far from Phetchabun? How long is the drive?
faq.a: From the Khao Kho–Lom Sak area to Phu Ruea is about 110–130 km, a 2–2.5 hour drive through Dan Sai. Then Phu Ruea to Chiang Khan is another 90–100 km, a 1.5–2 hour drive. It's beautiful mountain road but very winding, so drive during daylight.

faq.q: When is the mist at its best?
faq.a: November to January is peak season for the sea of mist and cool-weather flowers. Around 5–6 a.m. is the prime window for mist at Khao Kho, Phu Thap Boek, and Phu Ruea. But mist depends on the weather each day — some mornings the sky is clear and you see it well, some mornings you miss it.

faq.q: How much is the Phu Ruea park entry, and what are the hours?
faq.a: Phu Ruea National Park is open roughly 05:00–20:00. Entry is 200 THB for Thai adults, 100 THB for children, and 30 THB per car. To watch the sunrise at Pha Lon Noi, leave your accommodation before dawn.
